Walmart announces it will officially start supporting Apple Pay next week. The retailer had resisted offering Apple Pay for over a decade, despite ongoing pressure from customers.

Apple Pay finally arrives at Walmart

Walmart announced the news today in a press release. The company will begin rolling out contactless payment support, including Apple Pay, at select Walmart and Sam's Club locations starting August 24. The feature will cover all stores across the US by the end of this year, and will expand to gas stations by mid-2027.

Walmart is joining the broad contactless payment support, covering Apple Pay and Google Pay on iPhone and Apple Watch, contactless credit cards, and other payment platforms. Customers can also add membership cards for Walmart and Sam's Club to platforms like Apple Wallet. Contactless payments will operate alongside existing payment methods, including Walmart Pay.

The company stated:

Walmart is one of the last major retailers to still not support Apple Pay, making this significant news for consumers. For years, the retailer had refused to offer contactless payments, sticking with its QR code-based payment system, Walmart Pay.

Until last year, Walmart was doubling down on its belief that Walmart Pay was more convenient than Apple Pay. However, to use Walmart Pay, users must first add a debit or credit card within the Walmart app on iPhone, then scan a QR code at checkout to complete payment with iPhone.

A quick search on social media reveals users' frustration with Walmart's refusal to support Apple Pay.

After all, most retailers that long refused Apple Pay have caved in years ago, including Kroger, Home Depot, and H-E-B — and clearly for good reason.

Has Walmart's lack of Apple Pay support ever affected your shopping habits? With Apple Pay rolling out at Walmart and Sam's Club, will you be more inclined to visit? Let us know in the comments.
